title: Finite coefficient and Cartesian comparison calculus for a Tate source
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-pur-conventions]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $G_T=Lg_{T,\gamma}^*$, with $g_{T,\gamma}=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius $\gamma$ [def-pur-scheme-geometric-frobenius]. Work on the small pro-etale derived categories with $A=A_{E,n}$ and the operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be separated and finite type between such schemes, with geometric base change $f:X\to Y$ smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$. Write $F_f=Lf^*$, $T_{r,X}=A_X(r)$, and $P_fK=(F_fK\otimes^L T_{d,X})[2d]$. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ write $c_f:G_XF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_fG_Y$ for the canonical commuting-pullback comparison and
$$b_{f,K}=(c_{f,K}\otimes1)[2d]\,\mu_{g_X;F_fK,T_{d,X}}[2d]:G_XP_fK\xrightarrow{\sim}(F_fG_YK\otimes^LG_XT_{d,X})[2d],$$
where $\mu$ is the canonical pullback-tensor comparison [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], as in [def-pur-tate-datum]. Let $\varphi_K:G_YK\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ be a strict datum [def-pur-tate-datum] and put $\psi_{f,K}=(F_f\varphi_K\otimes\tau_{d,X})[2d]b_{f,K}$, with the canonical $\tau$ of [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists]. Let $(Q_X,Q_Y)$ be either derived reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$, $1\le m\le n$, or $(Lu^*,Lv^*)$ for the base change to $k$ of a Cartesian square of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes with vertical arrows $f_0,f'_0$ and horizontal arrows $u_0,v_0$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Primes denote the resulting coefficient/scheme data. Set $K'=Q_YK$, $C_T:Q_TG_T\cong G'_TQ_T$, $\varphi_{K'}=Q_Y(\varphi_K)C_{Y,K}^{-1}$, and let $a_P:Q_XP_fK\cong P'_{f'}K'$ be the canonical pullback, tensor, twist and shift comparison. Then, as maps from $Q_XG_XP_fK$ to $P'_{f'}K'$,
$$a_PQ_X(\psi_{f,K})=\bigl(F'_{f'}(Q_Y(\varphi_K)C_{Y,K}^{-1})\otimes\tau'_{d,X'}\bigr)[2d]b'_{f',K'}G'_X(a_P)C_{X,P_fK}.$$
The reduction case uses the finite-Tor comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. The square case uses only ordinary derived pullbacks; it makes no assertion of exceptional base change or of a Cartesian scheme-Frobenius square.

proof.text:
Put $F=F_f$, $F'=F'_{f'}$, $T=T_{d,X}$ and $T'=T'_{d,X'}$, and compose maps right to left. Write $A_M:Q_XFM\xrightarrow{\sim}F'Q_YM$, $t:Q_XT\xrightarrow{\sim}T'$, and $\nu_{M,N}:Q_X(M\otimes^LN)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_XM\otimes^LQ_XN$ for the canonical comparisons. For scheme pullback, $A$ is the natural isomorphism obtained by composing the two pullback-composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] around the given commuting square, and $\nu$ is the bifunctorial comparison of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. For reduction they are the pullback and tensor comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Naturality at $\varphi_K:G_YK\to K$ gives
$$A_KQ_X(F\varphi_K)=F'(Q_Y\varphi_K)A_{G_YK}.$$
All finite-reduction applications are on the finite-Tor domains already stipulated in the statement; the twist is a degree-zero invertible line. No direct-image comparison is used.

proof.text:
Apply the current statement of [lem-pur-canonical-tate-arrow-naturality] with $r=d\ge0$. In the square case take $T_0=X_0$, $T'_0=X'_0$, $w_0=u_0$, $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, so $Q_X=Lu^*$ and $t=t_{u,d}$. In the reduction case take $T_0=X_0$ and $R=Q_X=-\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$. The cited node writes its source exponent as $m$ and target exponent as $n$; substitute $(m_{\rm cited},n_{\rm cited})=(n,m)$, permitted by $1\le m\le n$. Thus $t=t_{R,d}$ and $C_R=C_X$ are precisely our canonical comparisons. The respective displayed scheme and coefficient equations both give
$$tQ_X(\tau_{d,X})=\tau'_{d,X'}G'_X(t)C_{X,T}.$$
This uses the actual roots-of-unity arrow, including its coefficient-unit case $d=0$. Put $\varphi'=Q_Y(\varphi_K)C_{Y,K}^{-1}$. Functoriality and cancellation give $F'(\varphi')F'(C_{Y,K})=F'(Q_Y\varphi_K)$.

proof.text:
Let $H=(FG_YK\otimes^LG_XT)[2d]$, $e=(F\varphi_K\otimes\tau_{d,X})[2d]:H\to P_fK$, and $e'=(F'\varphi'\otimes\tau'_{d,X'})[2d]$. Use $a_H$ as defined in [lem-pur-finite-tate-source-structural-coherence]. Suppress the canonical shift identifications temporarily. The definitions of $a_P$ and $a_H$ are
$$a_P=(A_K\otimes t)\nu_{FK,T},$$
$$a_H=(F'(C_{Y,K})A_{G_YK}\otimes G'_X(t)C_{X,T})\nu_{FG_YK,G_XT}.$$
Apply bifunctoriality of $\nu$ from [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] in the square case, or the tensor comparison of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] in the reduction case. Then the two factor equations of Steps 1 and 2 give
$$\begin{aligned}
a_PQ_X(e)
&=\bigl(A_KQ_X(F\varphi_K)\otimes tQ_X(\tau_{d,X})\bigr)\nu_{FG_YK,G_XT}\\
&=\bigl(F'(Q_Y\varphi_K)A_{G_YK}\otimes\tau'_{d,X'}G'_X(t)C_{X,T}\bigr)\nu_{FG_YK,G_XT}
=e'a_H.
\end{aligned}$$
Here each displayed expression is shifted by $[2d]$. Restoring the canonical termwise shift comparisons gives exactly the same equality, since the structural lemma states their compatibility. No tensor factors are interchanged.

proof.text:
By [lem-pur-finite-tate-source-structural-coherence],
$$a_HQ_X(b_{f,K})=b'_{f',K'}G'_X(a_P)C_{X,P_fK}.$$
Since $\psi_{f,K}=e b_{f,K}$, functoriality, Step 3 and this equation yield
$$a_PQ_X(\psi_{f,K})=a_PQ_X(e)Q_X(b_{f,K})=e'a_HQ_X(b_{f,K})=e'b'_{f',K'}G'_X(a_P)C_{X,P_fK}.$$
Substitute $e'=(F'_{f'}(Q_Y(\varphi_K)C_{Y,K}^{-1})\otimes\tau'_{d,X'})[2d]$. This is the claimed equality with precisely its stated source and target. The square case involved only ordinary pullbacks and their composition comparisons.

lean.statement: theorem finiteTateSourceComparisonReduction (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) {X₀ Y₀ : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of P.field.k₀))} (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀) (d : ℕ) [LocallyOfFiniteType f₀.left] [QuasiCompact f₀.left] [IsSeparated f₀.left] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d (P.frobeniusMap f₀)] (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hmn : m ≤ P.level) (K : Scheme.proEtaleDerivedCategory (P.frobeniusFiber Y₀).left P.Ring) (hK : finiteTorConstructible P.coefficients.l P.extension P.level P.level_pos (P.frobeniusFiber Y₀).left K) (φK : (P.finiteReductionPullback (P.frobeniusGaloisMap Y₀)).obj K ≅ K) : let QX := P.finiteReduction m hm hmn (P.frobeniusFiber X₀).left let QY := P.finiteReduction m hm hmn (P.frobeniusFiber Y₀).left let GX' := (P.finiteReductionSetting m hm).finiteReductionPullback (P.frobeniusGaloisMap X₀) let C_Y := P.finiteReductionPullbackComparison m hm hmn (P.frobeniusGaloisMap Y₀) K let φK' := C_Y.symm ≪≫ QY.mapIso φK let ψ := finiteTateSourceMap P f₀ d K φK let ψ' := finiteTateSourceMap (P.finiteReductionSetting m hm) f₀ d (QY.obj K) φK' let a_P := P.finiteReductionSourceComparison m hm hmn (P.frobeniusMap f₀) d K let C_X := P.finiteReductionPullbackComparison m hm hmn (P.frobeniusGaloisMap X₀) ((P.compositionShiftedPullback (P.frobeniusMap f₀) d).obj K) QX.map ψ.hom ≫ a_P.hom = C_X.hom ≫ GX'.map a_P.hom ≫ ψ'.hom
